Evidence and receipts

How Ringer verifies delegated work.

This page explains the difference between asking a coding agent for an answer and assigning work through a checked delivery contract.

RINGER RULE

Worker prose never decides PASS.

The declared check runs against the artifact. Exit zero establishes the mechanical result; PM still judges scope and outcome acceptance.

DIRECT CLI CALL

Prompt → answer

  • Worker chooses how to describe completion
  • Failure context may be partial
  • Artifacts and logs depend on the session
  • The caller must reconstruct what happened
RINGER ASSIGNMENT

Contract → attempt → gate → receipt

  • Owned paths and expected files are declared
  • Work runs in an isolated directory or worktree
  • The check executes after the attempt
  • Failure output feeds one bounded retry
  • Every attempt leaves logs and artifacts

Example record

A receipt is small enough to inspect.

It identifies the worker, attempt, revision, exact gate, result, and preserved evidence. A later manager or reviewer can understand why the artifact was accepted.

Ringer establishes that the declared gate passed. Ship acceptance establishes that the delivered outcome matches the accepted intent.

For interfaces

Receipts can contain observed UI evidence.

The ui-test plugin lets a Claude session dispatch Codex computer use through Ringer. Screenshots and on-screen reads return as typed evidence, executed checks validate the package, and a fresh verifier reads the captures before issuing PASS-OBSERVED, FAIL, or BLOCKED. See the UI testing page →
